date_note: Date is Security.nl's publication day; the AP's own publication date could not be read (its page returned 403).
title: Dutch data protection authority advises against buying camera glasses after tests
summary: Per Security.nl, the Dutch Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens advises people not to buy camera glasses after testing several models. It says some tested glasses had a serious vulnerability that let a nearby attacker take them over without the user's login details, and that only one of six had a noticeable recording light. It urges venue owners to ban them.
plain: The Dutch privacy regulator tested camera glasses and advises against buying them, citing a takeover flaw in some models and recording lights that protect bystanders too little, according to Security.nl.
exec: A regulator advises against camera glasses and calls on venue owners to ban them in house rules; review workplace and site policies.
action: Per the AP: do not buy camera glasses; owners and managers of locations should ban wearing and using them in their house rules.

validation.note: Security.nl and TechCrunch (independent publishers) both report the Dutch authority's advice not to buy the glasses. The AP original (autoriteitpersoonsgegevens.nl/documenten/ran-special-ai-camerabrillen-onder-de-loep) answered 403 and could not be read.
